parts.text:
5
One object moves directly from P to R.
R
Q
P
In a shorter time, a second object moves from P to Q to R.
Which statement about the two objects is correct for the journey from P to R?
A
They have the same average speed.
B
They have the same average velocity.
C
They have the same displacement.
D
They travel the same distance.

hints: Notice that both journeys start at P and finish at R, but one goes straight while the other detours via Q in a shorter time.
Recall that displacement is the straight vector from start to finish, while distance is the total length of the path actually travelled.
Recall that average speed uses distance and average velocity uses displacement, each divided by time, so check how the different path lengths and different times affect them.
walkthrough: Identify the given information: object 1 travels the straight segment P to R, object 2 travels the two segments P to Q then Q to R, and object 2 takes a shorter time.
State the rule for displacement: displacement is the vector from the initial position to the final position, with magnitude equal to the straight distance P to R and direction from P toward R.
Apply it here: because both objects start at P and end at R, their change in position is identical, even though the routes differ.
State the rule for distance and averages: distance is total path length, average speed $= \frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}$ and average velocity $= \frac{\text{displacement}}{\text{time}}$.

Compare: the P to Q to R distance is greater than the direct P to R distance, and the times are stated to be different, so neither average speed nor average velocity can be the same for the two objects.
Therefore only the quantity fixed by the common endpoints is equal. This is option C

A.explanation: Average speed is $\frac{\text{distance}}{\text{time}}$. The P to Q to R route has a larger distance but a shorter time, so the average speeds cannot be equal.

B.explanation: Average velocity is $\frac{\text{displacement}}{\text{time}}$. Displacement is the same but the times are different, so the average velocities are different.

C.explanation: Displacement depends only on start point P and end point R, so both objects have the same vector from P to R.

D.explanation: Distance is the total path length. The indirect path P to Q to R is longer than the direct path P to R.
